family: Deep Momentum Networks / Momentum Transformer / changepoint (CPD) tactic switching — Zohren group (Lim–Zohren–Roberts 2019 DMN; Wood–Roberts–Zohren 2021 Slow Momentum with Fast Reversion; Wood–Giegerich–Roberts–Zohren 2022 Momentum Transformer; Wood–Kessler–Roberts–Zohren 2023 X-Trend), plus the two independent 2024–2026 replications and the crypto-momentum literature that bears on it.
thesis: The tactic is a small sequence network f(u_t;θ) that emits a bounded position X_t^(i) = tanh(.) ∈ (−1,1) per asset from 8–10 hand features (vol-normalised returns at 1d/1m/3m/6m/1y + three MACD pairs (8,24),(16,48),(32,96); the CPD variant adds a Bayesian-GP changepoint severity ν_t and location γ_t over a 21–63-day lookback), trained by directly maximising the vol-targeted portfolio Sharpe, optionally with a turnover term inside the loss. The CPD variant 'switches' between a slow-momentum tactic (hold the trend) and a fast-reversion tactic (flip after a detected break). Decomposed against the four no-free-lunch sources: (1) FORECAST — dominant. The output is sign × magnitude of the conditional expected vol-scaled return; the Sharpe loss is merely a different estimator of the same conditional mean (it maximises E[X·r]/sd), and the CPD gate is a forecast of P(trend continues | recent break) — SMFR's own cost appendix attributes the gain to 'the fast reverting component', i.e. a short-horizon reversal forecast. (2) RISK PREMIUM — the TSMOM base carries the trend/crash-hedge premium the 819 book already carries and which reads ≈0 on this venue since 2024 (LEDGER 898). (3) REBALANCING/VOL PREMIUM — per-asset vol targeting σ_tgt/σ_t is a small vol-timing term; on this repo inverse-vol sizing measured −0.06 (PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md:49). (4) COST REDUCTION — the turnover regulariser and the attention model's longer memory are the only genuine 'tactics' content; in the papers they rescue a −5.3 Sharpe at 10 bp to +0.9, roughly the sign rule's +0.86, never far above it. Honest verdict: this family is a forecaster with good manners, and 'hold on policy' buys auditability, not expectancy. Its own published break-even is 2–3 bp per side; the repo charges 21.
math: Position: X_t^(i) = tanh(f(u_t^(i);θ)), u_t = [r_{t−k,t}/(σ_t√k) for k∈{1,21,63,126,252}, MACD(8,24),(16,48),(32,96) (, ν_t, γ_t)]. Strategy return (DMN eq. 1/35): R_t = (1/N_t) Σ_i X_t^(i) (σ_tgt/σ_t^(i)) r_{t+1}^(i) − c·σ_tgt·|X_t^(i)/σ_t^(i) − X_{t−1}^(i)/σ_{t−1}^(i)|. Loss (DMN eq. 16, SMFR eq. 14): L(θ) = −√252·mean_Ω(R)/sqrt(mean_Ω(R²)−mean_Ω(R)²). Repo cost identity (trader/backtest.py:188-190): net_c = gross − turn·c/1e4 per decision, so Sharpe_net ≈ Sharpe_gross − (ann_turn·c)/σ_book. Inputs from the 819 best cell (PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md:36): turn 0.155/day = 56.6×/yr, net@8 +1.09, net@21 +0.97 ⇒ Δcost 13 bp × 56.6 = 7.4%/yr for ΔSharpe 0.12 ⇒ σ_book ≈ 0.074/0.12 ≈ 61%/yr; drag per bp at 819 turnover = 56.6e-4/0.61 ≈ 0.0093 Sharpe/bp ⇒ the 21 bp tier costs ≈0.19 Sharpe (gross ≈ 1.16 survivor in-sample; PIT gross ≈ 0.75 given net@21 +0.56). DMN turnover in the literature: LSTM ≈ 10× Long-Only (DMN 2019 §VI); Pollok–Robik 2026 LSTM 0.17 vs TSMOM 0.02 one-sided/day (8.5×). At 8.5× the 819 turnover: 481×/yr × 21 bp = 101%/yr ⇒ −1.65 Sharpe of drag at σ 61%; at a regularised 3×: 170×/yr × 21 bp = 35.7%/yr ⇒ −0.58. Published cost slopes, 2015–2020 portfolio (MT Exhibit 10): TFT+CPD 2.00 @0 bp → 1.22 @1 → 0.44 @2 → −0.35 @3 (≈ −0.78 Sharpe/bp); LSTM 0.82 → 0.20 @1 → −1.05 @3 (≈ −0.62/bp); DMN 2019 LSTM 2.907 @0 → −5.313 @10 bp (≈ −0.82/bp). Under a matched-turnover and matched-gross constraint the second term cancels between arms, so the kill test below reduces to a paired gross-Sharpe comparison of the learned tactic against the frozen sign rule on the identical PIT panel and decision grid.

bear_positive_without_forecast.argument: The family's bear-positivity comes entirely from its short leg, i.e. a forecast that the downtrend persists. On this repo the 819 book's BEAR22 +1.10/+1.36 net@8 is carried by shorts: the long-flat variant reads BEAR22 −2.47 (LEDGER 898/trend-decay, line 103) and the leverage-matched long-only signal is negative in every regime. The CPD 'flip after a break' leg is a reversal forecast, not a tactic. The non-forecast components (vol targeting, turnover regularisation, DD throttle — trader/config.py:109-129) only rescale exposure; a rescaled zero-mean book has zero expected bear return, and vol-targeting pays only if returns are predictable from vol, which is itself a forecast (inverse-vol read −0.06 here, PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md:49). Pollok–Robik 2026 §E adds the failure mode: with a weak signal the Sharpe objective's natural solution is a steady sub-unit long exposure (their equity-index alpha is insignificant, β explains the return) — the opposite of BEAR-positive. The only tactic-like bear property in the record is relative: the 819 book beats B&H in every bear while being absolutely negative in 2026H1 (−1.66 vs −2.45), and the goalpost is absolute.

controllability: What 'hold on policy' buys here: the deployable object is a deterministic map from ~10 inspectable per-asset features to one bounded scalar X∈(−1,1); no search, no self-play, no learned world model. It can be tabulated (partial-dependence of X over normalised 1m/3m return and CPD severity), its variable importances are reported directly in the TFT variant (MT Exhibit 6: daily-return 23–31%, CPD features 4–9% each), and a single forward pass explains a trade. Against the MuZero policy (27-channel encoder over a strided close array, factored per-asset argmax, tree over inventory dynamics — jax_encoder/self_play receipts in the memo) this is categorically more auditable. Turnover is bounded only if you make it so: the literature's constraints are (i) a cost term c·σ_tgt·|X_t/σ_t − X_{t−1}/σ_{t−1}| inside the Sharpe loss (DMN 2019 eq. 35 — turns −5.31 into +0.91 at 10 bp; Pollok–Robik found it did not change rankings and over-constrained the low-turnover model), (ii) per-asset vol targeting σ_tgt/σ_t (15% in every paper; the repo's no-leverage Σ|w|≤1 rule replaces it — a real departure), (iii) tanh bounding of the output, (iv) validation-Sharpe early stopping, (v) 3–5-seed averaging (MT reruns 5×; Pollok–Robik: 'the only enhancement that reliably helps'), (vi) architecture choice — attention models trade ~8× less than the LSTM (0.02 vs 0.17 one-sided/day). Explicit position smoothing (EMA of X) or a no-trade band is practitioner practice, not in these papers; the repo's RiskConfig rebalance_band=0.002 is the analogue. What is lost: (a) there is no separable forecast to inspect — sizing and signal are fused in one output, the exact confound the direction memo diagnosed (§0.2) and which the Gârleanu–Pedersen route deliberately un-fuses; (b) the Sharpe objective can and does encode beta (Pollok–Robik Table IV: transformer equity α +0.8 n.s., β 0.63*), so 'holds positions' can be satisfied by a long-beta book that fails BEAR-positive; (c) hyperparameter/seed sensitivity is large (single-seed transformer 'not reliably distinguishable from zero'), so the auditability is per-seed-ensemble, not per-model; (d) the action space is continuous, so any rung that grades on the ±w_unit ladder must quantise it first.
compute: Small; this family does not need the 64 GB GPUs and barely needs a GPU at all. Papers: LSTM hidden 5–160, sequence 63, 8–10 features, 50–99 assets × 25–30 years (≈0.5–0.8M asset-days), 50-iteration random search × ≤300 epochs with patience 25 — minutes to a few hours per expanding fold on one small GPU or a multicore CPU; the TFT variant is hours per fold. The costly component is the GP changepoint precompute (GPflow, Matérn 3/2 + changepoint kernel, refit per asset-day per LBW): on this repo's PIT panel (≈273 assets × ≈2,800 daily rows ≈ 0.76M cells, two LBWs) that is ≈1.5M small GP fits ≈ CPU-hours to ~1 CPU-day parallel; an Adams–MacKay BOCPD (Gaussian, closed form) replaces it in seconds. Kill experiment total: 4 folds × 3 seeds × 4 arms × ≤10 HP draws ≈ ≤1 GPU-day on one 24 GB card or ≈2 CPU-days, safe_run-wrapped on gpu-server per .claude/rules/10; panel fits in RAM (<100 MB). Zero deploy, no env changes.

kill_experiment.design: Pre-registered row `9xx/dmn-cpd-tactic-kill`, SPEC hashed before the first score via the 898 `preregister`/`require_preregistered` pattern (decay_harness.py:308,:346). Panel: trader.data.load_db_backtest_panel(include_dead=True) PIT universe from build_pit_universe (trader/data.py:319, :426-453), true UTC daily bars, ohlcv_daily current to the 899 seam; universe/mask/warmup identical across arms (raise if not, as decay_harness.py:540-544 does). ARMS, all emitting pos[t,i] with Σ|pos|≤1 (repo no-leverage rule replaces the papers' 15% vol target): A0 control = frozen 819 sign(30d)/equal/H=1 via trader.strategy.positions_from_config. A1 = rule-based CPD switch, no learning (the SMFR thesis as a rule): Adams–MacKay BOCPD (Gaussian, hazard 1/λ, λ∈{60,120} declared) on each asset's vol-normalised daily return; if posterior run-length < k∈{5,10} days → reversal tactic (−sign of 5-day return) else trend tactic (sign 30d); equal weight. A4 = linear Sharpe-loss DMN (Lim 2019 'Linear-Sharpe'): ridge-regularised linear map of the 8 DMN features → tanh → position, trained on the Sharpe loss. A2 = LSTM DMN verbatim (8 features, hidden ∈{10,20,40}, seq 63, dropout, Adam, 300 epochs patience 25, 10 random-search draws on a validation Sharpe over the last 10% of each training window). A3 = A2 + CPD severity/location at LBW 21 and 63 (GP-CPD as SMFR, or BOCPD run-length posterior as the declared cheap substitute). FOLDS (expanding, strictly causal, purge 30 d): train 2018-10→2021-12 / test 2022 (BEAR22 form check); train →2023-12 / test 2024; train →2024-12 / test 2025; train →2025-12 / test 2026H1 (partial, n reported). 3 seeds per learned arm; seed median is the arm's number. MATCHING (declared, enforced before scoring, else the cell is 'UNMATCHED' and ungradable): each arm's realised ann_turn within ±10% of A0's on the same window (A0 ≈ 56.6×/yr; achieved by tuning the DMN turnover-regulariser λ on the validation window only, or by a declared EMA smoothing of positions) AND mean gross Σ|pos| within ±10% of A0's (renormalise to gross_cap=1). Exposure and ann_turn printed beside every Sharpe (898 Amendment-1 rule). ORDER: run A0, A1, A4 first (CPU-minutes). If A1 and A4 both FAIL by-year, A2/A3 are skipped and the family is recorded falsified — 811 and 819-CAPACITY both found nonlinear ≤ linear on these surfaces, and a nonlinear Sharpe-optimiser cannot recover what a linear one on the same features cannot; run A2/A3 only if A1 or A4 shows Δ>0 in ≥2/3 unseen years.

kill_experiment.pass_fail: FAMILY LIVES (goalpost band) iff, for A2 or A3 (or A1/A4 if they alone run), seed-median, matched turnover and gross: pooled unseen 2024-01→2026-06 net@21 ≥ +0.97 with bootstrap CI lo > 0, paired ΔSharpe vs A0 CI lo > 0, net@21 > 0 in ≥2 of the 3 unseen year-windows, BEAR22 fold net@21 > 0 and > B&H, gross ≥ 0.5 median with no >95%-flat days, terminal PV > 1. MARGINAL iff the same with pooled ≥ +0.56 (the PIT bar). FALSIFIED otherwise — including the case where every year-window CI includes 0 (the burden is on the new arm; 'can't reject' is FAIL for the family), and the case where the arm beats A0 only because A0 is negative while the arm's absolute net@21 ≤ 0 (record as 'beats a dead control', not alive). A UNMATCHED cell (turnover or gross outside ±10%) is not graded. Pre-committed consequence of FALSIFIED: H2 (docs/pathway.md:38) recorded as falsified for regime-conditional learned sizing on daily closes; no further DMN/CPD/regime-gating rows on the daily close surface; the Gârleanu–Pedersen predict-then-optimise row (memo §4) is unaffected either way.

Compute: A0/A1/A4 CPU-minutes; A2/A3 ≤ 1 GPU-day on one 24 GB card (or ≈2 CPU-days) for 4 folds × 3 seeds × 10 HP draws; GP-CPD precompute ≤ 1 CPU-day if used instead of BOCPD. Calendar ≤ 10 days from SPEC commit; kill date fixed in the SPEC. No deploy, no server env change, safe_run-wrapped per .claude/rules/10.

honest_odds: P(a DMN/CPD arm clears the PIT MARGINAL bar +0.56 net@21 with CI lo>0 on unseen 2024-01→2026-06 at matched turnover) ≈ 5%; P(clears +0.97 goalpost) ≈ 2%; P(paired Δ vs the sign rule > 0 with CI excluding 0) ≈ 10–15% — higher because the control itself reads +0.04 / +0.66 / −1.66 by year, so an arm that learns to sit near flat or short-beta in 2026H1 can beat it while failing the absolute bar. Reasoning: (1) the family's own break-even is 2–3 bp per side (DMN 2019), 2 bp (SMFR), ≈2.5 bp (MT+CPD portfolio); 21 bp is 7–10× that, and the cost slope is ≈ −0.6 to −0.8 Sharpe/bp in every published table — matched turnover removes the drag difference but the sign rule's own drag is already 0.19 Sharpe on a PIT gross ≈ 0.75; (2) the slow-momentum leg is the 819 signal, measured dead on this venue 2024–26 (LEDGER 898), and the DMN's information set is the same closes; (3) 819-CAPACITY and 811 found sequence/nonlinear models ≤ linear on this panel (GRU OOS IC 0.007/0.033); (4) the two sizing levers a DMN would blend read −0.06 and −0.16, and tanh conviction sizing −0.09 net@21, on the survivor panel where the signal was strongest; (5) the only independent replications (Pollok–Robik 2026 futures; Mason 2024 equities) show LSTM DMN < TSMOM net at 2 bp and the CPD variant not beating the non-CPD one, with 2022 ≈ 0 everywhere; (6) the Zohren group's own 2018–2023 zero-shot table has TSMOM −0.26 and DMN −0.11 at C=0; (7) 887/892 identify the attractors a Sharpe-loss net meets on a zero-EV signal: go flat, or destroy value in re-trims. Where the 5% lives: crypto's fast crashes (LUNA, FTX, 2026H1 whipsaw) are the one place a break-triggered fast-reversion leg could earn at daily horizon — and SMFR says that leg is the cost-fragile one; plus the record's regime-trigger test (813) was on minute data and n=6, so the daily CPD gate is not directly measured yet.
open_doubts: Whether a break-triggered fast-reversion leg has any daily-horizon analogue on Kraken crypto is unmeasured: 813's dissolved trigger map was minute-scale with n=6→25 events; 898's 2026H1 −1.66 for slow trend is consistent with whipsaw a reversal leg might catch. This is the one thing the kill experiment can genuinely learn.

The 819 lever attribution (invvol −0.06, ensemble −0.16, tanh −0.09) is single-config, in-sample, survivor-panel evidence; it makes learned sizing unlikely, not falsified — hence an experiment rather than a 'dead' verdict.

Replacing the papers' 15% per-asset vol target with the repo's Σ|w|≤1 no-leverage rule changes the family's shape; every published DMN number rests on vol targeting. The 819 book lives under the same rule, so the comparison is fair to the repo's question, not to the papers' claim.

Cost model is flat 21 bp/side on turnover with no rebalance band; the DMN's small daily re-trims are exactly the channel 892 found value-destructive. A declared band (RiskConfig rebalance_band 0.002) belongs in the SPEC as an arm parameter, not a post-hoc knob; the same applies to grading the existing RiskConfig overlay (TASK_820 gate-2 'turnover halved', Sharpe never reported).

No published DMN/CPD result exists at spot-crypto taker costs; every number I read is C=0 or ≤10 bp on futures/equities. Absence of evidence, not evidence of absence — the reason to run the cheap kill rather than rule by literature.

Power: 2026H1 has ≈180 decisions and 898's calendar-year CIs are ±2 Sharpe wide; the experiment can fail to reject. The SPEC pre-commits that 'every window CI includes 0' is FAIL for the family, so the outcome is decidable, but a true small edge (< +0.5) is undetectable by design.

Depth caveats: PMC12404547 (PLOS One 2025), arXiv 2602.11708 (crypto AdaptiveTrend), Grobys 2025, IJFE 2026 and arXiv 2603.01820 were read at abstract/summary level only; the five Zohren-group/replication papers and their tables were read in full via extracted text.

Sharpe as the loss and the metric on crypto momentum returns with power-law realised variance (IJFE 2026) may be statistically ill-posed; the repo's block-bootstrap CI is the mitigation, and terminal PV must be printed beside every Sharpe.
